question.text:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Z \sim N(0,1),$ compute $P(-2.20 \lt Z \lt 2.10).$

$z$$\, 0.00 \,$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$
$\, -2.2 \,$ $\, 0.0139 \,$ $\, 0.0143 \,$ $\, 0.0146 \,$
$\, -2.1 \,$ $\, 0.0179 \,$ $\, 0.0183 \,$ $\, 0.0188 \,$
$\, -2.0 \,$ $\, 0.0228 \,$ $\, 0.0232 \,$ $\, 0.0239 \,$
question.explanation:
We're given that $Z\sim N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(-2.20 \lt Z \lt 2.10).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $\Phi(z),$

\[ P(Z \leq z) = \Phi(z). \]

So, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$:

\[ \begin{align*} P(-2.20 \lt Z \lt 2.10) &= P(Z \lt 2.10) - P(Z \leq -2.20) \\[5pt] &= P(Z \leq 2.10) - P(Z \leq -2.20) \\[5pt] &= \Phi(2.10) - \Phi(-2.20) \end{align*} \]

From the table, we know that

\[ \begin{align} \Phi(-2.20) &= 0.0139, \\[3pt] \Phi(-2.10) &= 0.0179, \end{align} \]

but we are not given $\Phi(2.10).$ However, we can compute this using symmetry:

\[ \begin{align*} \Phi(2.10) &= P(Z \leq 2.10) \\[5pt] &= 1 - P(Z \leq -2.10) \\[5pt] &= 1 - \Phi(-2.10) \\[5pt] &= 1 - 0.0179 \\[5pt] &= 0.9821 \end{align*} \]

Therefore, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P(-2.20 \lt Z \lt 2.10) &= \Phi(2.10) - \Phi(-2.20) \\[5pt] &= 0.9821 - 0.0139 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 0.9682 }. \end{align*} \]
